quest.title: Thalia and Melpomene
quest.description: Trace and find the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's seals.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

chapter.num: In the Wake of Narcissus: Act I
chapter.title: Search in the Algae Sea

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: This is the last place.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: At least the entrance is still sealed.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Looks like Jakob hasn't answered the riddle here.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Perhaps he provided "an" answer, just not "the" answer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... The answers from before were "shadow," "life," and "love."

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Based on the previous patterns, my logic module has hypothesized the tablet inscription to be as follows:

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: "Always united"... "Born in an instant, often contradicting, I accompany you in eternal rest"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then the last line is "the first droplet."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Caterpillar, Seymour, do you guys know the answer?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I think I have an idea concerning "the first droplet."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It sounds like it's referring to the first raindrop that fell following the creation of the world. I believe this idea was in vogue with both Ancient Fontaine and the Ordo.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But how are we supposed to find something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well, this first droplet became part of all water in Teyvat. In that sense, every drop of water is the "first droplet."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's like the first god spreading out the potential for greatness. An element of divinity is present in every person's body.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if it's that simple, the person who came before us should have had no problem offering up the right answer.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Indeed. I'm probably wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Well, even if it was the wrong answer, it was a good one. I can only conclude that the person who set up these riddles had no sense of romance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And now he's laughing at you for not getting how security works!

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I am unable to provide an answer. My search for "the first droplet" retrieved 1,200 results.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: "Legend has it that the world's first drop of wine came to be when the Anemo God..."

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Very well.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: About that... I think I have something I can share.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: There's a legend that says that Oceanids came from the first tear shed by the previous Hydro Archon.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Meanwhile, the first tear on the earth was shed by the first Oceanid after she came to understand humanity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wouldn't the first tear in the world have come from the first crying human baby?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Animal tears are actually salt discharges, and in those peaceful times, humans breathed their first in laughter.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: That's what the legends say, anyway.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Actually, I believe that the cries of babies and animal salt discharges can be regarded as similarly unemotional behaviors.

response.speaker: Seymour
response.text: Babies cry due to external stimuli, and to fill their lungs with air as quickly as possible. That is what the Sumeru Amurta textbooks say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is the answer an "Oceanid" then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That does seem like an answer that the person before us might not have provided.

choices.text: I think you're beating a dead horse here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks this is the right track, though!

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Based on my understanding of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, this makes logical sense.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: The Red Empress who dreams in a place unknown, the dreamer who never says what they mean.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's even more confusing than the riddles.

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: Well, does that matter? We're already at the final juncture. Whatever the case, the answer will come to light at the end.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Now then, Ann, if you wouldn't mind.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Sure, I'll give it a try. But do come up with another answer quickly if I fail, alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It opened!

response.speaker: Caterpillar
response.text: We have to get the last piece. Otherwise, the Holy Blade will fall into the Ordo's hands.

choices.text: I think we're on the right track!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure beats trying to find the Anemo God's wine!

choices.text: We can give it a shot. Let's go to Mondstadt...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you're gonna flog a dead horse, let's at least go about it the right way!

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: This is the last place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Our search hasn't turned up anything so far...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Very true. However, this entrance is shut, which means we still have a chance.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Looks like our adversary hasn't solved the riddle here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That said, who *is* our competition, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Assuming that the Narzissenkreuz Ordo has been inactive for centuries and that the knowledge I possess of it still holds true, combined with events that occurred prior to now...

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I fear it must be Jakob.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: That jerk who was picking on Seymour? What would he want with this stuff...?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: I'm afraid that his objective is the same as ours — to find the materials needed to forge the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The Ordo was able to reproduce the four requisite hypothetical substances here in the material world, based on the esoteric philosophies of the underground kingdom and Ancient Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I do not understand.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: These enigmatic substances are purely experiential. You could say they are even further beyond ordinary logic than elemental power.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: I entered all introductory to intermediate level textbooks from the Akademiya's Spantamad into my memory banks decades ago. There is nothing mysterious about elemental power.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Is that so? Anyway, to sum up, this is born of the confluence of traditions from Fontaine and technology from the ancient underground kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: And thus, four types of substance came into being: Memory, Wish, Soul, and Persona.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: To avoid any possible ambiguity, let's call them the "Memory" piece, "Wish" piece, "Soul" piece, and "Persona" piece.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are these used to make the Holy Blade?

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: In the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's brand of mystical philosophy, the temple is a microcosm of the universe, the members are stand-ins for the gods, and the holy oil is tempered willpower.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The Holy Blade, on the other hand, is "reason," that which cuts everything open. It can only be born out of consummate human will.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Quite abstruse.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: That's esotericism for you. You attach yourself to anything that looks similar enough, and when this sort of thing becomes magic, fiction becomes reality.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Either way, our adversary hasn't yet solved the riddle. Or he did, but wasn't able to provide the correct answer. With Jakob being said adversary, my bet is on the latter.

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: The inscription here reads: "Always united"... "Born in an instant, often contradicting, I accompany you in eternal rest"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And the last line is "the first droplet."

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: The areas from before had riddles like this as well. Do you guys still remember the answers?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Shadow."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Life."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Love."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, the answers just keep getting more abstract, don't they?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Caterpillar, Seymour, do you guys know the answer to this riddle?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Is that the "Persona" piece ahead?

dialogues.speaker: Seymour
dialogues.text: Unable to analyze the density of the substance before us. It appears to have a mass of... zero.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It looks like we've got the last piece. We should at least be able to negotiate a bit with our opposition now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: On the bright side, at least we can stop the Narzissenkreuz Ordo from forging the Holy Blade.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Not at all, Paimon. Our final goal is to forge the Holy Blade ourselves, and use it to stop their plan.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: Of course, Ann, I have not forgotten what this sword means to you.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: A Holy Sword that can cut out the will is also your key to unraveling the mystery. And to be honest, it is equally important to me as well.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: It's just that we have more important, more pressing matters at hand. Would you mind, then, if we looked into the mysteries surrounding us later?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I'm fine with that.

dialogues.speaker: Caterpillar
dialogues.text: #In that case, {NICKNAME}, please take this "Persona" with you, if you would.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is the area up ahead the final one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'd better get a move on.
I suppose I can take this to mean that you've accepted our invitation.

dialogues.text: What's happening!?
